chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi' who said:

I asked him, meaning Aba Ja'far عليه السلام, about something from the matter of the Imam, and I said: 'Can the Imam be a son less than seven years old?' So he said: 'Yes, and even less than five years old.'
So Sahl said: 'Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated this to me in the year two hundred and twenty-one.'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, the Imam being referred to
key_terms.أَمْرِ: the matter or affair under discussion
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely appointed Imam being discussed

ai.seo_question: Can an Imam be younger than seven years old according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the question of the Imam's young age and affirms that the Imam may be less than seven years old, and even less than five years old. It is significant in discussions of the Imamate, indicating that divine authority is not restricted by ordinary expectations of age.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about something from the matters of the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and I said, ‘Can the Imam<sup>asws</sup> happen to be a boy of less than seven years old?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and even less than five years old’.
So Sahl said, ‘Ali Bin Mahziyar narrated to me with this during the year two hundred and twenty one (A.H.)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ who has said the following.

“I asked abu Ja‘far (a.s.) of an issue of the Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority) and I said, “Can the Imam be a boy less than seven years old?” He said, “Yes, he can even be less the five years old.”
Sahl has said that ibn Mahziyar narrated this to me in the year two hundred twenty one.”
